name: Vantablack Media Somatic Noise Cloak
description:
The Somatic Noise Cloak is a wearable signal disruption garment — a full-torso vest and sleeve assembly lined with Vantablack's proprietary Stochastic Emission Fabric, which generates a continuously randomized electromagnetic emission profile that mimics the ambient background noise of GLMZ's densely saturated wireless environment. Rather than blocking or absorbing signals, the SNC actively broadcasts low-power noise across a broad spectrum, causing the wearer's electronic footprint to dissolve into the city's background chatter. Biometric sensors, passive RFID sweeps, and short-range identity interrogation systems read the wearer as environmental noise rather than a discrete target.

The garment's intelligence layer is a thin-film processor woven into the collar assembly that samples the local EM environment every 200 milliseconds and adjusts the emission profile to match. In high-traffic commercial zones, the SNC produces a denser, more complex noise signature; in quieter industrial or residential areas, it scales back to avoid the paradox of being the loudest silent thing in the room. Vantablack calls this the Ambient Calibration Loop, and it represents the company's most sophisticated application of their media-disruption research to a physical product. The vest is warm, slightly stiff, and has a faint electrical smell that users report fading after several wears.

The SNC was originally developed for Vantablack's own field journalists and embedded documentary crews operating in corporate-controlled zones where press credentials are selectively enforced. Its availability on the open market — at significant cost — reflects Vantablack's philosophy that information freedom is a consumer product. Corporate security contractors have lobbied unsuccessfully to have it classified as prohibited equipment; the current licensing requirement is enforced inconsistently at best.

specifications.effective_against: Passive RFID sweep, biometric sensor arrays, short-range identity interrogation, standard wireless tracking
specifications.limitations: Does not defeat active millimeter-wave scanning or hardwired biometric systems

tactical_use: Worn during transit through surveilled public spaces, corporate campuses, or controlled-access zones where passive identity scanning is routine. Most effective when combined with physical disguise and behavioral discipline — the SNC defeats electronic identification but does nothing for visual recognition. Used by journalists, runners, and anyone who needs to move through a monitored environment without leaving a trackable electronic record.
cultural_context: The Somatic Noise Cloak has become a minor status symbol in GLMZ's civil liberties and anti-corporate activist communities, where wearing one is a political statement as much as a practical choice. Vantablack has leaned into this positioning, sponsoring events and embedding SNC imagery in their media content. Corporate security firms have responded by developing active scanning systems specifically designed to detect the Ambient Calibration Loop's characteristic emission signature — an arms race that Vantablack's engineers appear to relish. On the street, the garment's stiff profile and electrical smell make it recognizable to anyone who knows what to look for.
story_hooks: A runner wearing an SNC discovers they are still being tracked — someone has developed a counter-detection system tuned specifically to the Ambient Calibration Loop's signature, and Vantablack hasn't issued a patch.
A dead activist is found with an SNC still active on her body — the garment's emission log contains a compressed record of every wireless environment she passed through in her final 18 hours.

Vantablack is quietly recalling a specific firmware version of the SNC after discovering the calibration processor was compromised during manufacturing — the affected units have been broadcasting a covert identifier to unknown receivers.

A corporate security director wants a runner to acquire an SNC from a Vantablack field journalist without alerting Vantablack — the journalist has been documenting something that hasn't been published yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: A fitted tactical vest with integrated sleeves, appearing as a high-tech compression garment. The surface has a subtle, almost liquid quality — not quite matte black, with fine iridescent shimmer across the Stochastic Emission Fabric when light catches it at certain angles. The weave pattern is visible up close: dense, interlocking conductive threads embedded in a dark synthetic base. Sleek, intentionally non-descript design that reads as expensive minimalism rather than armor.
physical_description.dimensions: Vest spans 45cm chest-to-shoulder depth, sleeves extend 60cm arm length. Compact enough to layer under a jacket but substantial enough to feel like a full torso system.
physical_description.weight_description: Light but present at 1.1kg — handheld-category weight, worn as a garment. User feels the consistent pressure across the torso like a weighted compression shirt.
physical_description.primary_material: Stochastic Emission Fabric: proprietary conductive composite weave with base synthetic polymer. Appears black with anthracite undertones.
physical_description.finish: Satin-smooth with micro-texture grip at the weave level. Faint opalescent shift under direct light — hints of violet and deep blue reflections that suggest the conductive thread lattice beneath. Slightly stiff initially, becomes supple with wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: pure black (Vantablack-adjacent, near-total light absorption). Accent: slate grey piping on shoulder seams and sleeve cuffs. Subtle maroon/burgundy undertones visible only in direct light, suggesting circuitry pathways.
physical_description.interface_elements: Slim collar-mounted control node (7cm × 4cm) with three tactile pressure points (power, mode cycle, diagnostic). Tiny recessed indicator LED cluster (status: white/amber/red) at collar base. Inductive charging contact points disguised as subtle metallic pads on inner left shoulder. Minimalist fabric label at upper back seam bearing SABLE Content Forge branding.
distinctive_features: Nearly imperceptible shimmer across the entire surface caused by conductive thread lattice
Collar-mounted thin-film processor visible as a slightly raised, geometrically precise rectangle of fractionally different texture
Shoulder seam piping that houses the Ambient Calibration Loop antenna array
Faint electrical scent (reported to fade after 3-5 wears) — not unpleasant, like ionized air after rain
Almost no visible hardware or external ports; all integration is seamless and recessed
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: SABLE Content Forge logo (stylized Φ-shaped mark) embossed on collar inner label. Regulatory compliance stamps (GLMZ Class-3 Utility, Vantablack Patent Lic. 2219-X4) in minimal white print on back neck seam. Serial number on inner cuff in micro-etched format.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn under casual wear or tactical jacket in urban environments. With use, the initial stiffness decreases and the fabric develops a lived-in patina. No visible degradation; the Stochastic Emission Fabric is designed for 3+ years of continuous wear. Users often wear it directly over baseline skin or light thermals. Small wrinkles and body conformity are normal; the garment molds to its wearer over time.
